thread:
ivy: ran into another onboarding hiccup — user trying to set up the JS quickstart kept getting `TypeError: require(...) is not a function` when using `require('redwood-inference')`.

ben: what Node version? sometimes old node + conditional exports cause funky resolution.

ivy: node 14 in their CI. they also tried `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'` and `new Redwood()` which threw `TypeError: Redwood is not a constructor`.

docs-eng: okay this is the usual default vs named export confusion + CJS/ESM mismatch. we only show `import { Client } from 'redwood-inference'` in quickstart which assumes ESM. need explicit CJS docs.

sasha: suggested copy: "If your project uses CommonJS (Node < 12, or `require()`), use the CJS entrypoint: `const { Client } = require('redwood-inference/cjs')`. For ESM or modern bundlers use `import { Client } from 'redwood-inference'`. Do not `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'` — the SDK exports named symbols, not a default export."

ben: also call out that some hosts (Vercel Edge, Cloudflare Workers) are ESM-only and have no `process`/`global` — point them to the edge bundle: `import { Client } from 'redwood-inference/edge'`.

ivy: user also hit bundler polyfills getting pulled in (node-libs-browser) which increased bundle size and caused runtime failures. we should suggest tree-shaking and direct edge import.

docs-eng: plan: add a short "Import styles & runtime" section in the quickstart with a tiny table: runtime -> entrypoint -> example. plus a short FAQ "Why does `require('redwood-inference')` not work?"

ben: we should also include an example showing the shape of the CJS export so people stop guessing: `console.log(require('redwood-inference/cjs')) // { Client: [Function: Client], version: 'x.y.z' }`. that's quick and helps debugging.

sasha: TypeScript note: for ESM consumers `import type { ClientOptions } from 'redwood-inference'` works. For CJS + TS users show JSDoc style: `/** @type {import('redwood-inference').ClientOptions} */ const opts = {}`.

ivy: can we add tests? a small smoke test that runs the CJS example on CI would catch regressions. also an edge smoke test (deploy preview with edge import) would be ideal but more infra.

devx-bot: Created issue RW-DX-619: "docs(js): clarify CJS/ESM imports, edge entrypoint, and add smoke tests" - https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/619

docs-eng: I'll open the docs PR today. ivy can you add the sample-app CJS smoke test? ben, can you look at package.json exports map to ensure conditional `require()` resolution works on older Node?

ben: on it — I'll audit `exports` and add a note in changelog if we change resolution behavior. also add a brief line in release notes recommending `require('redwood-inference/cjs')` for older Node.

ivy: adding sample-app PR now: test will `node cjs-smoke.js` where `cjs-smoke.js` contains `const { Client } = require('redwood-inference/cjs'); console.log(typeof Client)`. will assert `function`.

sasha: docs-eng, when you PR, include both short snippets and the troubleshooting checklist: 1) What import style are you using? 2) Are you in Edge/Serverless? 3) Try `/cjs` if `require` fails.

devx-bot: PR template updated to remind authors to include both ESM and CJS snippets for JS SDK docs.

ivy: thanks all — this should reduce the 1:1 support tickets. will paste PR links once they exist.
